reviews.body:
### 🟡 Changes recommended Closing a gzip/deflate dataset can race with an active read because the decompressor is closed before the HTTP body without synchronizing with the read.
1 open issue - [Synchronize decompressor cleanup with active reads](https://github.com/Azure/azure-kusto-go/pull/364#discussion_r4548668089) · New
What changed in this PR Addresses #359 by making iterative query dataset closure close the underlying response reader, so stalled reads can be interrupted without cancelling the original request. **Changes:** - Retains the frame reader and closes it from `IterativeDataset.Close()`. - Uses `sync.Once` to prevent repeated underlying close calls. - Adds a regression test for stalled-read interruption and single-close behavior. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `azkustodata/​query/​v2/​iterative_dataset.go` | Connects dataset closure to response-reader cleanup. | | `azkustodata/​query/​v2/​iterative_dataset_close_test.go` | Tests stalled reads and repeated closure. | | `azkustodata/​query/​v2/​frame_reader.go` | Makes reader closure idempotent and preserves its error. |
Review effort: Balanced

### 🟡 Changes recommended The shutdown path relies on undocumented concurrent Read/Close guarantees, risking races or blocked compressed reads, and can incorrectly report shutdown-induced read errors as failures.
2 open issues - [Document or support concurrent read interruption on Close](https://github.com/Azure/azure-kusto-go/pull/364#discussion_r4585691236) · New - [Avoid reporting shutdown-induced compressed read errors](https://github.com/Azure/azure-kusto-go/pull/364#discussion_r4585691281) · New
1 resolved since last review - [Synchronize decompressor cleanup with active reads](https://github.com/Azure/azure-kusto-go/pull/364#discussion_r4548668089)

review_comments.body: Closing a gzip/deflate dataset while `advance()` is reading can race inside the decompressor: `response.originalCloser.Close()` closes it before the HTTP body. `sync.Once` only serializes close calls, not reads. Make the wrapper close the HTTP body first, synchronize decompressor cleanup with completion of the active read, and add compressed-response race coverage.

When `Close` overlaps a pending read, this assumes the caller-supplied `io.ReadCloser` supports concurrent `Read`/`Close` and that closing it interrupts the read. The public constructor documents neither requirement, and a raw `*gzip.Reader` can race without unblocking its underlying stream. Provide a transport-level interruption path, or explicitly document the stronger reader contract on `NewIterativeDataset`.

When this interrupts a stalled gzip/deflate read, `originalCloser.Close` returns the induced read error, so an otherwise successful dataset shutdown now reports failure. Keep closing the reader while preserving the previous nil result (or filtering shutdown-induced errors), and add a compressed dataset test that checks the return value.

comments.body:
Addressed the compressed-response cleanup concern: the transport closes first, active reads finish before decompressor cleanup, and repeated closes share the same result. Added gzip/deflate stalled-read coverage and a close-order regression test; both affected packages pass under the race detector.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
